items.title: Ray Bauduc and Nappy Lamare Interview, 1959-09-09
items.q: That was including Benny Goodman in the band. They had Jack Teague on and Jimmy McPartland and Big Braider's on piano... I think Dick Morgan was playing banjo and guitar there and Harry Goodman on bass... Gil Roden and Benny Goodman and Larry Binion, I think, was the first saxophone player when I jo

ctx.x: I listened to him on those records. There's one thing I wanted to ask Ray was telling us the other night, if we don't take all your intermission either, but a little bit about the... a little bit about the two beat, like we were talking about down beat again, and the Crosby period saying that all Dixieland is two beat rhythm. And you were explaining the other night that that's the wrong idea. Oh, well, it isn't the wrong idea.

It's just that everybody has the idea that Dixieland is a two beat rhythm. And that that was brought out. The fact that music came along and progressed a little bit as far as when Benny Goodman came in, he kept a full beat ride. Yeah. And the magazine, like the Metronome and the down beat, they came along and they didn't know how to decipher Dixieland. So they called it two beat and Benny Goodman's style was four beat. Yeah. But as far as Dixieland, the actual beat of Dixieland to me is not two beat. It's on the…
